\section{Discussion and Conclusion}
\label{sec:discussion}

\paragraph{Limitations.}\looseness=-1
Our conclusions rest on $N{=}2$ independent VLM-to-VLA transitions (TraceVLA, NORA) plus one VLA-to-VLA case (OpenVLA), all causal-decoder architectures evaluated on a single benchmark (LIBERO); flow-matching~\cite{black2024_pi0} and diffusion~\cite{ghosh2024_octo} action heads may produce different routing structures.
All findings are correlational: probe $R^2$ reflects decodability, not causal reliance, and confounds from data distribution and optimization cannot be ruled out.
The correlation between trained $\Delta R^2$ and published success rates ($\rho{=}0.583$, $p{=}0.10$; Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_discussion_appendix}) is underpowered ($n{=}9$), though the effect size is large ($|\rho|{>}0.5$).
Each architecture is analyzed at a single checkpoint, precluding characterization of how exit collapse develops during training; the three-tier gradient has $n{=}1$ at Tier~2 (OpenVLA), limiting its inferential power.
All analyses are open-loop, consistent with prior representational studies~\cite{grant2026,haon2025}; closed-loop behavioral validation, intermediate-checkpoint dynamics, and extension to additional architectures and benchmarks are priorities for future work.

\paragraph{Conclusion.}\looseness=-1
We present a first cross-architecture decomposition of instruction routing in VLAs, identifying a consistent three-way pattern---entry gating, mid-layer integration, and exit collapse---across three architectures, two training pathways, and four instruction conditions.
$\Delta R^2 > 0.10$ provides a probe-based screening signal that can supplement rollout evaluation, and mid-layer features (peak at L9--L11) outperform exit-layer representations where collapse is pronounced (Appendix~\ref{sec:extended_practical_implications}).
Code and data will be released upon acceptance.
